Swapnil Tripathi

PhD researcher, Electrical & Computer Engineering, University of California, Santa Cruz

I explore new converter topologies, specializing in hybrid switched-capacitor converters — proposing them, designing the hardware, and testing it in the lab. The work targets high-density, high-frequency power conversion spanning kilovolt-class buses down to 48 V, for data center, space, and aerospace applications. My M.S. at IIT Madras covered multilevel inverter topologies, capacitor voltage balancing, and motor drives.

What I work on

Hybrid switched-capacitor converters

Converter control
Proportional-resonant current control, PLL grid synchronization, digital implementation on C2000 DSP and FPGA

800 V → 28 V GaN hybrid switched-capacitor converter

A stacked-Dickson hybrid switched-capacitor stage merged with a multi-phase buck regulator, built for high-voltage space and aerospace power distribution. The multilevel switch stack holds per-device stress to a fixed fraction of the bus, so 150 V GaN HEMTs run from an 800 V input, and resonant charge redistribution imposes ZVS across the Dickson stage.

I owned the build end to end: topology analysis, device and magnetics selection, schematic capture, 4-layer Altium layout, assembly, and bench validation.

An enhanced resonant charge recovery clocking scheme that pre-energizes the resonant inductor ahead of each commutation, taking the front-end 2:1 stage from the partial ZVS of prior art to complete ZVS. It is a control and timing contribution: no added hardware.

The pre-energization current and interval come from an LC energy-balance argument, verified on a 1 MHz prototype with a symmetric dual-inductor hybrid Dickson stage and a dense flying-capacitor bank on the reverse side of the board.

Grid-tied inverter control

Feb – Jun 2025

Project associate, IISc Bengaluru, with Prof. Vishnu Mahadev Iyer.

Proportional-resonant current control with PLL grid synchronization on a Nova converter for a grid-tied energy storage application. I developed the loop in firmware, tuned it against the plant model, and closed it in hardware, including real and reactive power control for stable grid integration.

Multilevel inverter topologies and motor drives

2022 – 2025

M.S. thesis research, IIT Madras, with Prof. Srirama Srinivas.

rating
10 kVA
DC bus
>400 V
motor
1.5 kW IM
control
DSP + FPGA

Capacitor voltage balancing PWM for a single-DC-source cascaded H-bridge multilevel inverter driving an induction motor. I implemented carrier-modified PWM and field-oriented control on a TMS320F28377S and Xilinx FPGA platform, then commissioned and debugged the drive on the bench. The work produced two published IEEE papers.

Inverter hardware for Formula Racing and Hyperloop

2022 – 2025

Team Raftar Formula Racing and Team Avishkar Hyperloop, IIT Madras.

For Raftar, a collaboration with Daimler Trucks, I designed the sensing and signal conditioning board for a 5 kW PMSM inverter and a 10 kVA Si-IGBT gate driver with active Miller clamp, dead-time control, and short-circuit protection.

For Avishkar, I mentored the H-bridge hardware for the electromagnetic levitation module, which competed at European Hyperloop Week.
